title: refactor(auth,components,react)!: burn ledger batch 5 — 18 symbols stop wearing spec names (#3159)
body:
Closes objectui#3159 (do not auto-close until merged). Part of objectstack#4115 — debt-ledger burn-down, batch 5 of 8.

Eighteen symbols across `@object-ui/auth`, `@object-ui/components` and `@object-ui/react` were declared under names `@objectstack/spec` already owns. **Ledger 62 → 45, 17 → 14 packages** — all three packages leave the ledger entirely.

## Verdicts

Twelve derive, five rename, one goes to ALLOW — and one needed no fix at all.

### `@object-ui/auth` (6)

| symbol | verdict | why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `TenancyPosture` | **re-export** | member-for-member identical to `@objectstack/spec/security` |
| `DelegableScope` | **re-export** | identical, including the element type the local copy spelled out inline — `DelegableAdminScope` comes along |
| `AuthUser` | **derive** (`extends`) | same concept, and the copy was **losing keys** — see below |
| `AuthSession` | **rename** → `AuthClientSession` | spec models the SERVER session record; this is the browser's token bundle |
| `AuthProviderConfig` | **rename** → `AuthProviderOptions` | spec owns that name for the OAuth registration `{id, clientId, clientSecret, scope?}` |
| `AuthProvider` | **ALLOW** | a React context provider component vs a zod enum of provider ids |

`AuthUser` is the one worth reading. The local declaration never had the spec's `positions` or `tenantId` — the authorization inputs — and its `[key: string]: unknown` index signature made that invisible **both** at every call site and to any structural comparison (the objectstack#4075 mechanism: an index signature absorbs anything, so `[Local] extends [Spec]` answers "identical" no matter how far apart they are). It now `extends` the spec principal, so the display-only fields (`image`, `role`, `roles`, `emailVerified`) are the whole delta and a new spec field arrives on its own.

`AuthSession` is the counter-case, and the rename is load-bearing in both directions: the spec requires `id`/`userId` the client never sees and types `expiresAt` as an ISO string, while this holds a JS `Date`, requires `token`, and carries a `refreshToken` the spec has no concept of. Mutually unassignable — a re-export would have been a silent contract swap wearing a burn-down's clothes.

**`AuthProvider` vs `AuthProviderConfig` is deliberately a split verdict**, and the reason is the failure mode this issue is about rather than a general rule about components. Nobody mistakes `<AuthProvider authUrl=…>` for a `z.ZodEnum` of provider ids, and renaming it breaks the React `<XProvider>` convention and every consumer's JSX for no defect. Its *config type* is the opposite: same domain, same words, and `AuthProviderConfig` in the spec is the OAuth registration shape — exactly the symbol the next session reads as canonical. So the component is excused with a written reason and a tripwire; the type is renamed.

### `@object-ui/components` (6)

| symbol | verdict | why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ShareLinkPermission` | **re-export** | byte-identical hand copy |
| `ShareLinkAudience` | **re-export** | byte-identical hand copy |
| `ShareLink` | **derive** | the spec row minus `password_hash`, plus the boolean projection |
| `SortItem` | **derive** (`extends`) | the spec's `{field, order}` plus a synthetic React key |
| `FilterCondition` | **rename** → `FilterBuilderCondition` | see below |
| `Field` | **rename** → `FieldContainer` | a React wrapper `<div>` vs the spec's object-FIELD metadata |

**`FilterCondition` was triaged here, not inherited.** The cross-package guidance on this name has now been wrong once in each direction, so it is worth stating what all of them actually are:

| where | what it is | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/spec/data` | recursive ObjectQL predicate AST (`$and`/`$or`/`$not`) | — |
| `@object-ui/app-shell` | that same AST, but declared as `Record<string, any>` | re-export (objectui#3169) |
| `@object-ui/types` | one flat FilterBuilder row | renamed `FilterBuilderCondition` (objectui#3068) |
| **`@object-ui/components` (this PR)** | **one flat FilterBuilder row** — `{id, field, operator, value}`, `operator` drawn from the builder's own `FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS` dropdown vocabulary, not the spec's `$`-tokens | **renamed `FilterBuilderCondition`**, matching `@object-ui/types` |

Copying app-shell's verdict would have replaced a flat builder row with a recursive query type; copying types' verdict *is* right here, but only because reading both confirmed it. Same name, two different objects, two different answers.

`ShareLink` omits `password_hash` rather than marking it optional: it is the credential itself, and typing it in a browser package is an invitation to render it. `password_protected` is the one local addition. `created_at` is widened to `| null` to match every other timestamp on the spec's own row.

`Field` had **no importers at all** — it was public API by way of `export * from './custom'` and nothing consumed it, so the rename costs nothing and removes a name that means "an object field's metadata" everywhere else on the platform. `@object-ui/app-shell` already renamed the same kind of collision (`FieldInput` → `ScreenFieldInput`) for the same reason.

### `@object-ui/react` (6)

| symbol | verdict | why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `OfflineStrategy` | **re-export** | identical |
| `ConflictResolutionStrategy` | **rename → the spec's own name**, `ConflictResolution` | see below |
| `OfflineCacheConfig` | **derive** (input side) | `.default()`ed keys must stay authorable |
| `OfflineConfig` | **derive** (input side) | see below |
| `NavigationConfig` | **derive** (input side), `mode` required | one documented narrowing |
| `PerformanceConfig` | **no fix needed** | the spec RETIRED the name in 17.0.0-rc.1 |

`ConflictResolutionStrategy` is the batch's sharpest trap. That name **is** a spec export — in `@objectstack/spec/api`, where it means the metadata-MERGE policy (`error | priority | first-wins | last-wins`). The union this hook actually uses (`manual | client_wins | server_wins | last_write_wins`) is the spec's `ConflictResolution`, in `/ui`. Deriving under the old name would have produced a symbol whose name points at one union and whose value is another. The fix takes the spec's own name **and** its binding in one step — the same move as `FieldGroup` → `ObjectFieldGroup` in objectui#3169.

**`OfflineConfig` keeps its name here.** That was a cross-package call: `@object-ui/types` had an `OfflineConfig` too, but it turned out to be a service-worker *route* cache and has been renamed `PWAOfflineConfig` (objectui#3156). This hook's config is the spec's concept key for key, so it takes the spec's binding — no dialect.

**`PerformanceConfig` needed nothing.** `PerformanceConfigSchema` / `PerformanceConfig` were retired from `@objectstack/spec/ui` in 17.0.0-rc.1, so the collision ended on its own and the name is objectui's now. Pinned anyway, because "the spec dropped it" is a claim with an expiry date: if the spec re-adds the name, the tripwire fails and the symbol gets re-triaged rather than silently becoming a fork. **The keys still exist inside the spec** (`virtualScroll`, `debounceMs`, … appear nested under `@objectstack/spec/api`), so this may be a move rather than a retirement — flagged below.

## Method notes worth carrying forward

**1. Derive configs from the schema's INPUT side, and the tell is in the hook signature.** `useOffline(config: OfflineConfig = {})` defaults to the empty object. `z.infer` makes every `.default()`ed key required, so the output type rejects the default the hook ships with. `@object-ui/react` has no `zod` dependency (it renders plain objects and never parses), so rather than adding one, `packages/react/src/spec-input.ts` reads the input type off the schema's own `_zod` internals — the spec's binding, no new dependency, no copy of the shape.

**2. Two "kept local to avoid a dependency" comments, both false.** `useNavigationOverlay`'s copy said *"inline … to avoid importing from `@object-ui/types` (which may not be a direct dependency of `@object-ui/react`)"* — but the vocabulary belongs to `@objectstack/spec`, which **is** a direct dependency. Same shape as the app-shell comment objectui#3169 found. And `useOffline` / `usePerformance` both claimed alignment with *"@objectstack/spec v2.0.7"* against an installed 17.0.0-rc.1.

**3. Every candidate new name was run through the guard before use.** `AuthClientSession`, `AuthProviderOptions`, `FilterBuilderCondition`, `FieldContainer` — all free. (`ConflictResolution` is taken, which is the point: it is a re-export.)

**4. A byte-faithful re-fork passes every parity assertion.** Demonstrated in the mutation testing below — this is why the guard, not the tests, is the mechanism for type-only symbols.

## Verification

- **Ledger** — `--ledger` regenerated after blanking the block (the parallel-batch conflict recipe), then set-diffed against `origin/main`: **removed** = exactly the 17 symbols this batch burns (`PerformanceConfig` was already off main's ledger, the spec having retired it), **added** = none, **every other package byte-identical**. 62 → 45, 17 → 14 packages.
- **Guard** — green: `1202 files scanned against 4344 spec export names; 9 declared dialects, 45 untriaged collisions in 14 packages`.
- **Type-check** — `turbo build --filter` on the three changed packages to rebuild their dists **first**, then `turbo type-check --force`: **78/78**, including `apps/console`. (Per objectstack#4115's own note: per-package `tsc` otherwise resolves the *old* dist and reads green.)
- **Lint** — 0 errors across the three packages.
- **Tests** — full suite green: **9511 passed / 25 skipped / 0 failed** across 813 files, including the three new parity suites (37 assertions).
- **Renames were grepped in test files separately**, because test files are excluded from every package tsconfig and so a green `type-check` proves nothing about them.

### Mutation testing — four directions, all red

| mutation | what fired |
|:--|:--|
| re-fork `TenancyPosture` as a **byte-faithful** hand copy | guard, by name + file (`types.ts:33`) |
| undo the `FilterCondition` rename | guard, by name + file (`filter-builder.tsx:39`) |
| leave a burned name (`SortItem`) in `DEBT` | guard's rot ratchet — "lists 1 symbol in DEBT that no longer collide" |
| delete the `AuthProvider` ALLOW entry | guard, as a fresh collision |

The first is the one worth recording. With the import removed so the copy compiles cleanly, **`pnpm type-check` passed and the parity test passed 14/14** — a hand copy identical to the spec satisfies `Assert<Equal<Local, Spec>>` exactly as well as the real binding does. For a type-only symbol there is no reference identity to check (unlike objectui#3169's `isAggregatedViewContainer`, where `expect(local).toBe(spec.x)` catches it), so **the guard is the only mechanism that can tell a derivation from a faithful fork.** The parity tests pin the *shape* of a deliberate divergence; they cannot detect a copy.

### Compile-time pins are actually compiled

All three parity tests carry `Assert<Equal<Local, Spec>>` pins, and this branch originally shipped them unchecked — every package tsconfig excludes `**/*.test.ts`, and CI's only type gate drives those configs. objectui#3187 landed the fix for that pattern while this branch was in flight, so this adopts its convention rather than the root-level project written here first: a per-package `tsconfig.typetests.json` with an explicit include list, chained from each package's `type-check` script (enforced by `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`). That guard now reports **4 packages with a narrow type-assertion project**, up from 1.

## Left for someone to decide

- **`PerformanceConfigSchema`'s disappearance** — retirement or a move? The keys still exist nested under `@objectstack/spec/api`. If it moved, `usePerformance` should derive from wherever it landed instead of keeping the local declaration.
- **The guard only walks `packages/`.** `apps/console/src/pages/shared-record-shape.ts` declares its own third `ShareLink` — with `audience: string`, so any misspelt audience is invisible there. Out of scope for a ledger batch (the ledger is packages-only), but it is the same defect one directory over, and objectui#3074 already found that `apps/` consumers are easy to miss.
- **`@objectstack/spec` moved from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` in `@object-ui/components`**, since its public type surface now references the spec. Flagging in case that package is meant to stay spec-free — the import is type-only and erases from the JS, but the emitted `.d.ts` references it.
